extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of mechanics, history, and philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Historical and methodological guidelines about how investigators in mechanics (Archimedes, Stevinus, Galileo, Huygens, etc.) used experiment, thought-experiment, idealization, decomposition/composition, and conceptual formulation to discover and justify mechanical laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments are never absolutely exact, but they at least may lead the inquiring mind to conjecture that the key which will clear up the connexion of all the facts is contained in the exact metrical expression PL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments can suggest correct mathematical forms (e.g. PL) even if measurements are imperfect; they are the means by which conjectured forms are tested. Examples: Stevinus's inclined-plane considerations and Archimedes/Galileo deductions become intelligible only under such hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought experiments (mental experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not essential that the experiments should have been actually carried out, if the result is beyond question of doubt. As a matter of fact, Stevinus experiments in thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mental experiments may validly substitute for physical experiments when results are self-evident or when physical disturbances (friction, etc.) can be idealized away. Examples: Stevinus's chain thought-experiment; Archimedes' lever reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idealization and neglect of disturbing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact static relationship is reached by idealisation and disregard of these disturbing elements. The lever and the inclined plane are self-created ideal objects of mechanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use idealized models (ideal lever, frictionless planes) to attain exact relationships; recognize that real devices approximate ideals only to the extent disturbances are minimized. Physical experiments approach the ideal as disturbing factors are reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior conception determines experimental form
rubrics_metrics.description: Without some preconceived opinion the experiment is impossible, because its form is determined by the opinion. The experiment confirms, modifies, or overthrows our suspicion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments guided by prior hypotheses or conceptual sketches; experiments do not arise in a vacuum. Expect an iterative cycle: hypothesis → experiment → confirmation/modification/overthrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid circular reasoning / do not assume the result
rubrics_metrics.description: Archimedes makes the action of two equal weights to be the same under all circumstances as that of the combined weights acting at the middle point ... the particular form of dependence of the moment on L is implicitly determined by what has been done ... the entire deduction contains the proposition to be demonstrated, by assumption if not explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully inspect transformations and assumptions so they do not covertly import the conclusion. Avoid procedures that presuppose the law one seeks to prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry limits inference of functional dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: If the arrangement is absolutely symmetrical in every respect, equilibrium obtains on the assumption of any form of dependence whatever ... the particular form of dependence PL cannot possibly be inferred from the equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to infer the functional form of a physical dependence from equilibria that are symmetric enough to be indifferent to that form; seek asymmetric tests or additional assumptions to determine dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer general hypotheses over special-case reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Stevinus reached the very general view that a mobile, heavy, endless chain of any form stays at rest ... Stevinus, although he too doubtless knows approximately, at least, what he is in search of, nevertheless could have found it directly by his manner of procedure ... Archimedes' case is the most special conceivable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from general, robust principles when possible (higher value) rather than from narrowly tailored special cases that may implicitly use the result. General approaches often permit direct deduction of many special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of particular results with the whole (philosophical treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The habit which great inquirers have of bringing their single conceptions into agreement with the general conception or ideal of an entire province of phenomena...A truly philosophical treatment of any special science will always consist in bringing the results into relationship and harmony with the established knowledge of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate new findings to the broader body of knowledge; use coherence with established theory as a criterion to reject fanciful or abortive theories. Cross-check isolated results for compatibility with the general picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation and superposition (decomposition and composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decomposition of phenomena into mutually independent parts has been aptly characterised...isolation, and the composition of a phenomenon out of such parts, superposition. The two processes combined enable us to comprehend...what, as a whole, it would be impossible for us to grasp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze complex phenomena by isolating independent factors and studying them in 'purity', then reconstruct the whole by superposition. Examples: Galileo's decomposition of projectile motion; Newton's parallelogram of forces; Fourier's composition of thermal disturbances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual formulation and abstraction from sensory impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: For scientific purposes our mental representations of the facts of sensual experience must be submitted to conceptual formulation. This formulation is effected by isolating and emphasising what is deemed of importance, by neglecting what is subsidiary, by abstracting, by idealising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert qualitative sensory impressions into precise mathematical or conceptual forms (e.g., ask 'Of what is v a function?'). Use abstraction to focus on essential variables and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments test the adequacy of chosen theoretical forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiment determines whether the form chosen is adequate to the facts. The experiment confirms, modifies, or overthrows our suspicion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat experiments as arbiters of whether a proposed functional form or law matches reality; be prepared to refine or abandon forms that fail empirical tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for disturbing circumstances in empirical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviation increases with the disturbing circumstances, as with friction, and decreases with the diminution of these difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize sources of experimental error (friction, other disturbances); design experiments to minimize or control them to approach ideal theoretical predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of perceptual/time-scale illusions in interpreting phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Freely falling bodies are followed with more difficulty by the eye the longer and the farther they have fallen;...We fail to observe any descent in the initial part of the curve, and forget to take into account the shortness of the corresponding time of the descent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze timescales and measurement resolution to avoid being misled by appearances (e.g., initial segments of projectile paths, rotating chains appearing rigid). Supplement observation with analysis or instrumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical contingency: new laws may be initially unclear and refined gradually
rubrics_metrics.description: The law of inertia did not possess in Galileo's mind the degree of clearness and universality that it subsequently acquired...His hesitation in enunciating in its most general terms a law that at first blush appears so startling, is not surprising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect that breakthrough ideas can be imperfectly formulated at first; value gradual clarification, critique, and refinement across investigators and time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple demonstrative experiments to probe nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Anaxagoras proves the corporeality of the air by means of closed inflated tubes, and from the gathering up of the expelled air...Philo of Byzantium employs for the same purpose an inverted vessel having in its bottom an orifice closed with wax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ straightforward, reproducible demonstrations to test hypotheses about material properties (e.g., air's corporeality, vacua between particles). Such elementary experiments can persuasively establish physical principles.
